title: The Phone Call Home
setting: Monday night. 10:30pm. You're at your kitchen table writing a code-review comment. Your phone lights up. AMMA. You answer in your mother tongue — the language of every meal, every fight, every birthday — and you don't even think about it. After you hang up, you sit there a long moment.

beats.native: Hi kanna. ate already? You sound tired.
beats.translit: (in your mother tongue, soft and unhurried)
beats.en: Hi, child. Have you eaten? You sound tired.
beats.beat: your mother's voice — the one that knows what you sound like at every age

choices.en: Yeah Amma, ate. Tired but okay. Got a new project at work today.
Yeah, just finishing up. Long day.
I was going to call you, I swear.

beats.native: Your father planted three new roses today. He's been asking when you'll come home for a weekend. The new flat is nice? Cook is good?
beats.translit: (she's not the type to push, but she's keeping a list)
beats.en: Your father planted three new roses today. He's been asking when you'll visit. Is the new flat nice? Is the cook good?
beats.beat: the careful checklist of a mother who can't visit

choices.en: Flat's great Amma, you'd like it. Cook is excellent. Met her daughter today — she's doing well in school.
All fine. Hectic. Promise I'll send pictures.

beats.translit: (quiet, casual, the way she asks everything important)
beats.beat: the question lands like she's been holding it for two weeks

choices.en: Maybe. Met someone last week. Anika. She's — she's good, Amma. I'll tell you more soon.
Working too much for that, Amma.

beats.native: Okay okay. Don't keep too many secrets. Sleep early — you sound tired. I'll call Sunday.
beats.translit: (she's not going to push tonight. she just wanted to know.)
beats.en: Okay okay. Don't keep too many secrets. Sleep early — you sound tired. I'll call Sunday.
beats.beat: she hangs up before you can argue about anything

beats.native: You set the phone down. You realise for the last twenty minutes you'd been switching to English from a language you'd already started thinking in. Kannada. The shift wasn't loud. It just happened.
beats.en: You set the phone down. You realise for the last twenty minutes you'd been switching to English from a language you'd already started thinking in. Kannada. The shift wasn't loud. It just happened.
beats.beat: the chapter's only line of true narrator. no choice after. the realisation is the chapter.
